scope: Durable content AI receipts and recovery in the existing generateAuraContent callable and CourseEditor consumers.
behavior: Reuse the existing nutrition AI transaction coordinator with a separate auraContent operation and server prompt/schema/model-policy fingerprint.

A request identity shares one quota charge and one provider-generation workflow across duplicate requests and instances while its durable receipt remains available. Provider dispatch intent is recorded before network I/O; ambiguous outcomes never trigger automatic regeneration.

Legacy clients without request IDs use a deterministic server fingerprint. New clients persist an account/action/payload request ID and use a separate read-only request-status action after reload or an uncertain transport response.
Recovery checks status at most 12 additional times only when the server reports processing. There is no idle or background polling and no cross-region fallback.

An explicit new draft creates and durably stores a new request ID before invocation. Invalid local state, an expired missing receipt or an old-server response never silently starts another generation.
Current authorization is checked before replay, within a new claim and after generation. Owner changes fence browser invocation, waiting and late responses.
Stable generated item IDs prevent duplicate recovered quiz and memory items while retaining existing edits. Late results cannot modify another course or a draft edited while generation was pending.
The existing provider-rejection-only model fallback and quota limits remain in place. No release workflow, Rules, runtime settings, indexes or Academy workbook protocol changes.

storage.browser: Request identifiers and state only; no prompts or generated results.
storage.server: Owner-scoped fingerprint, state, lease and completed response, with existing seven-day expiresAt TTL policy.
storage.ttlPolicy: ACTIVE, read-only verification at 2026-10-25T05:28:39.573Z; no new policy or business data writes.

validation.fullLocalCi: passed; final missing-completed-receipt guard also passed the affected client and actual-service suites
validation.fixtures: Actual Firestore emulator transactions and actual frontend service/editor with synthetic callable/provider transport.

tradeoffs: Receipts add Firestore reads, writes, temporary response storage and TTL deletions. Replays avoid another provider call but still read current authority and the receipt. Currency savings are not measured.

Idempotency is bounded by receipt retention and identity continuity. Provider-internal retries or billing are outside this guarantee. Old and new clients can use different default IDs; no cross-version universal deduplication is claimed.
An unknown provider outcome stays read-only. Users may explicitly create another draft knowing it is a new generation; there is no automated recovery that could charge twice.
Missing local storage still supports deterministic default IDs, but arbitrary new-draft IDs require durable local storage. Clearing local state or losing receipts limits recovery.
A changed server prompt/model policy conflicts with a prior request fingerprint instead of silently rerunning it. An explicit new draft is required.

rollout.requires: Complete the coordinated Academy handoff and PR28/30/31/32 cutover; then deploy and verify only generateAuraContent from this reviewed source before merging this frontend.
rollout.rollback: Restore the previous frontend first. Retain the new compatible backend so pending receipts remain recoverable; reverting the backend removes durable recovery semantics.
